checks.summary:
Final Opus review of the merged diff 2d86b77..HEAD on claude/fervent-wozniak-rlk7su. I did a code review and ran targeted backend tests. I did no browser control/HEAD replay, so the "control" fields say n/a.

Verdict: nothing blocking. All 15 items are in the merged code, and every claim in /home/user/pt4/fix_groups_result.json that I checked exists. Robert's six decisions are built in full and none of the earlier decisions was undone.

Seams between the groups:
- The release route calls release_from_campaign, so a release or leave drops Train dice as a retire does. End Assignment keeps them through end_assignment_for, and gm.py:371 is the only caller of end_assignment_for.
- drop_report removes the report together with its new note.
- The not-filed line, the key tally, the "N of M" count and the Lightkeeper's Circle Relationships paper all read circleCreation.activeInvestigators, reports and relationships. The investigator_released handler replaces all of these, and votes_dict always sends every vote type, so the votes merge replaces them correctly.
- finalize_roster now locks the circle. The lock order is the same as gm_return_spend (character, then circle), so there is no deadlock.
- #54 only re-signs rows with author_type gm and no character, so a released member's entries keep that member's name.
- Probe: when the target of a Behind Me offer leaves mid-offer, the ally's answer is refused (403, no mark moved) and the lapse line is logged.
- Probe: a released ally whose socket reconnects without a campaign can still take the old Doctor's Non-Combatant drive point (nerve went from 1 to 2). This is a nit.

Protocol and pins:
- investigator_released is documented in WEBSOCKET.md (35 types), FRONTEND.md and ROUTES.md.
- The route is pinned in test_surface.py, test_00_startup.py, test_access.py (45 routes) and openapi.json.
- submit_assignment_report gains an optional note field (422 when it is too long or not text). The offer and lapse lines are plain activity_log frames.
- The QUIRKS-pinned tests were flipped, not deleted (test_gm_end_assignment, the notebook/account author tests, test_spend_refresh_and_train), and every test name QUIRKS cites exists.

Em dashes and model names: the only em dashes in added lines are the two kept '[Well-Read — n Intuition refunded]' log strings (nit). No model name appears in any file. The only one is in the required commit trailers.

Tests: on my own database (final_review_t1, dropped afterwards) I ran test_00_startup, campaigns, rest_broadcasts, ws_circle, ws_marks, account, notebook, ws_chat_notebook, investigators, surface, access and ws_rolls.
- First run: 1240 passed, 2 failed. One failure is test_cors_allows_configured_origin_only, because CORS_ORIGINS is not set outside the harness. The other is the new test_a_non_combatant_point_is_logged_... test, which is flaky.
- Second run: 1200 passed. The 6 errors were only caplog, which I had turned off with -p no:logging.
- test_ws_marks.py alone passed twice (101 each).
- In a smaller run, a pre-existing drain-timing assertion in test_ws_circle.py:484 also flaked once.
- vite build of HEAD succeeds; output went to the scratchpad, and the working tree is clean.

Issues: two should-fix (the Train/release wording in the docs and confirms, and the flaky new timing tests) and five nits.

items.item: #49 release a member / leave a campaign (decision 1)
items.fixed: POST /campaign/release/{id} (campaigns.py:356). The owner or the campaign's Lightkeeper may call it; it is refused with 409 for pending, dead or free investigators. It locks the character and then the circle, frees the character as Retire does (release_from_campaign) and keeps the row. It deletes the votes and the relationships at both ends, then drops the report (drop_report). After the seal lower_resources_to_pool lowers each pool and never raises one; before the seal _announce_members_changed fills them. It broadcasts investigator_released (named copy to the Lightkeeper, plain copy to the members, short copy to the investigator's own key), then circle_update, then a log line with no reason. Frontend: a two-press Release on the Lightkeeper's sheet (GMCharacterSheet ReleaseMember), Leave on the desk (LeaveCampaign) and on the hub's registry row with no Leave for the dead, armed lines that say what happens, and a store handler on every desk. There is no Release on the roster card itself; the card opens the sheet, and the decision says 'card or sheet'. Tests pass.

items.item: #50 Train die kept until used, spend wording (decision 2)
items.fixed: end_assignment_for no longer clears train_bonus/train_dice, and the spend count still resets. Retire and release drop the dice through release_from_campaign. 'kept until a roll uses it' appears on the card, in the log line, on the roll chip, in RESOURCE_HELP, on the sheet badge (the Lightkeeper's sheet too) and on the Circle page rule ('up to two each assignment, whenever the Lightkeeper opens spending'), and in FAQ, QUIRKS, WEBSOCKET, ROUTES and RULES_CHECK. test_gm_end_assignment was flipped. FAQ.md:277 still says only retiring drops the dice (see issues).

items.fixed: serializers.py sends `or 0` for all three maximums. InvestigatorDossier uses `?? 0` and shows 'none' with no pips for a 0 maximum; gameStore postRollChoiceWaiting uses `?? 0`. test_a_drive_maximum_of_0_is_sent_as_0 passes.

issues.item: #50 x #49 seam: Train dice and the rest of the reset on release are not described
issues.problem: release_member runs release_from_campaign (campaigns.py:384). That drops the investigator's bought Train dice and clears its gear, ability uses and spend count. FAQ.md:277 still says only 'retiring the campaign does, for each investigator it lets go'. The FAQ release answer (line 169) and both armed lines list votes, relationships, report and pool, but never say the player loses any Train die they hold. Decision 1 asks both confirms to 'say what will happen', and decision 2 asks for one consistent description of when a Train die goes.
issues.fix: FAQ.md:277: '(retiring the campaign, or releasing or leaving, does)'. FAQ.md:169: add 'its assignment ends as at Retire: spends, ability uses, gear and any Train dice it held are cleared'. Optionally add ', and any Train die they hold is lost' to leaveHint and the ReleaseMember armed line when character.train_bonus is set. Add the same note to the QUIRKS.md retire line.

issues.item: #59 new timing tests are order and timing dependent
issues.problem: test_a_non_combatant_point_is_logged_for_the_lightkeeper_and_that_ally_and_its_lapse_too failed once in my 1242-test targeted run. It passed in four other runs: alone, twice in test_ws_marks.py on its own, and in the 1200-test rerun. It asserts the exact order of the two 'is offered' lines, but _offer_non_combatant's allies query (and _intercept_allies) has no ORDER BY, so Postgres heap order decides. It also relies on a 1.5 s window, which a loaded run can overrun before the ally answers. The organiser's full suite can go red at random.
issues.fix: Add .order_by(Character.id) to the allies queries in _offer_non_combatant and _intercept_allies (this also gives stable log order at the table). In the test, raise the window (for example to 5 s with a recv_type timeout to match) or compare the offered lines without regard to order.

issues.problem: Both rewritten Well-Read lines add an em dash ('[Well-Read — {back} Intuition refunded]'). The rule is no em dashes anywhere. The group kept it because frontend/src/game/outcomes.js matches that format with a regex.
issues.fix: Accept it as an existing machine-read token, or change the format and the outcomes.js regex together in a later round (and the '[gilded — ...]' and 'used Train — ...' strings with it).

issues.item: #49 x #59: a released ally keeps the old campaign's Non-Combatant point
issues.problem: In my probe the Doctor took a mark, the Lightkeeper released the ally, and the ally's desk reconnected with no campaign. resolve_ability_mark Non-Combatant then still raised that ally's Nerve 1 to 2. The access check skips sockets without a campaign, and release does not clear _non_combatant[char.id] as close_offers_at_death does.
issues.fix: In release_member, after the commit, pop marks._non_combatant (and _pending_rush) for the released character, as close_offers_at_death does. Or refuse the Non-Combatant answer from a character that is not an active member of a campaign.

issues.item: #49 spend count reset on leave and rejoin
issues.problem: Release zeroes resources_spent_assignment. A player who has spent both spends can leave and come back in the same assignment, with the same or a new investigator. If the Lightkeeper approves, they have two fresh spends, because only an active predecessor's count is carried. Earlier decision: spends follow the player, and a replacement keeps its predecessor's count.
issues.fix: Robert's call. Either accept it, since the Lightkeeper's approval gates it, or keep the count on release (reset it only at End Assignment) and say so in FAQ.

issues.item: #49 x #58: report submitted at the moment of a release
issues.problem: The access check passes, the release commits (drop_report finds nothing), and then submit_assignment_report takes the circle lock and stores a report for an investigator who is no longer a member. It does not check membership again under the lock. The window is very narrow, and the desks' tally ignores non-members, but the row stays in backstory_answers until End Assignment.
issues.fix: Under the lock, refuse with 403/409 when reporter.status != 'active' or reporter.campaign_id != camp_id.

issues.problem: spend_resource takes no lock on the circle. A spend that read Train 6 before a release lowered it to 5 writes 5, so one spend is lost against the new maximum. This existed before the branch (spend against spend); the release makes one more writer.
issues.fix: Optional: db.refresh(circle, with_for_update=True) before reading cur_val, as the tally and spend-back handlers do.

checks.summary: All six items replayed in Chromium on control 2d86b77 (API 8032, site 4032) and HEAD f31e7c8 (API 8031, site 4031, build /tmp/build_main4). Each server had its own fresh database, and tables were built over the API with the verifiers' setups. Control reproduced every problem. HEAD fixes #52, #54, #56, #57 and #60 at the original device sizes and the neighbouring ones I tried. #53 is only partly fixed. On desktop and laptop every Contents line now brings its entry into view and focuses it. A 1366x629 window pages one line at a time and every line can be reached. On a 390x844 phone, though, the first entry on a spread is scrolled under the sticky desk header, so its title is hidden. Control left that title visible. I count this as a blocking regression. Other checks: Escape on a label, editing an existing label with the Text tool, the pen after labels, and saving to an entry all work. The startup step re-signs a username-signed Lightkeeper row as 'The Lightkeeper', and a socket-path Lightkeeper entry is also signed 'The Lightkeeper'. On HEAD no WS frame or HTTP body seen by a player carries the login name. The relationships paper updates live on accept and counter (the counter flips 'waiting for' to the proposer) and keeps them after a reload. The session-ended notice shows on the hub (401) and on the Lightkeeper's and a player's desk (4401), clears on a good sign-in, and also works on a phone. The join notice is in the first person on 1920, tablet and phone. No page errors in any run. Servers stopped by PID (5315, 5318, 5344, 5352 and their wrapper shells). Databases bc_notebook_session_head and bc_notebook_session_ctl dropped. Scripts and screenshots are in /tmp/bc_notebook_session (shots/ctl_* and shots/head_*). Nothing in the repo was edited.

issues.where: frontend/src/components/shared/NotebookView.jsx showEntry (about line 630) with EntryCard scroll-mt-28; phone 390x844
issues.problem: On a phone, a Contents line for the first entry on a spread scrolls the window so the card sits at y=0. Its title (0 to 80px) is under the 89px sticky desk header and log strip, and the page label and Contents ribbon scroll away. Seen with the bell tower sketch, entry 7, the first card of spread 2. The second and third cards land correctly at y=112. The card is the first child of the page's own overflow-y-auto div, which is a scroll container even on phone. Chrome clips the 112px scroll-margin rect to that container, so the window aligns the card's own top to 0. Control left this title visible at y=253, so the fix made the phone case worse for a third of the lines. Tablet 820 also lands at 0 but has no sticky header there.
issues.fix: Below lg, scroll the window explicitly instead of relying on scroll-margin. For example: const y = card.getBoundingClientRect().top + window.scrollY - (sticky header height + 16); window.scrollTo({ top: y }). Alternatively make the page's inner div overflow-y-auto only at lg (lg:overflow-y-auto), so the window is the only scroller on phone. Check the first entry of a spread on 390x844 again.
